semantic_fragments.content: Clause 13.2: For ME equipment and ME systems intended to actively keep alive or resuscitate a patient, reducing the auditory alarm signal volume below audible levels was not possible, except when the alarm system was connected to a distributed alarm system that included generation of auditory alarm signals per IEC 60601-1-8:2006 and IEC 60601-1-8:2006/AMD1:2012. Result: See attached IEC 60601-1-8 Report. Verdict: N/E.

Clause 8.4 RM RESULTS TABLE for interruption of power supply is marked N/A with supplementary information: Not life supporting ME equipment or ME system. This means the requirements for power supply interruption for life-supporting equipment do not apply.

Shock test conditions per IEC 60068-2-27:2008 (Clause 10.1.2a): Peak acceleration 150 m/s² (15 g), Duration 11 ms, Pulse shape half-sine, Number of shocks 3 per direction per axis (18 total). This represents Class 7M1 as described in IEC TR 60721-4-7:2001. All six directions (+X, -X, +Y, -Y, +Z, -Z) passed with basic safety and essential performance maintained.

Broad-band random vibration test per IEC 60068-2-64:2008 (Clause 10.1.2b): Acceleration amplitude profile: 10 Hz to 100 Hz at 1.0 (m/s²)²/Hz; 100 Hz to 200 Hz at -3 dB per octave; 200 Hz to 2000 Hz at 0.5 (m/s²)²/Hz. Duration: 30 min per perpendicular axis (3 total). All three axes (X, Y, Z) tested with 3 runs each, all passed with basic safety and essential performance maintained.
